item.content:encoded:
A massive Ukrainian attack on Novorossiysk. Day 1637 of the war

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-08-25

Russian forces have made further minor advances in Donetsk Oblast, where four main lines of attack have taken shape: a broad front from the east towards Sloviansk and Kramatorsk; from the south-east and south-west towards Druzhkivka and on to Kramatorsk; from the south and east towards Dobropillia; and from the north and east towards Lyman and on to Sloviansk. Only in the Lyman area have Ukrainian forces managed to hold back Russia’s advance relatively effectively and for a sustained period, posing a threat to the westernmost part of its force group, which is separated from the rest of its forces by the Netryus River. The Russians have destroyed a further two bridges over the Kazennyi Torets River in Sloviansk, further isolating the Ukrainian force in its eastern sector and on the outskirts of the town from its rear. The bridges on the northern and southern banks of Sloviansk, as well as on a tributary to the west of the town centre, remain intact. Sloviansk, Kramatorsk and Druzhkivka are under constant bombardment and shelling.

item.content:encoded:
Following Beijing’s lead, the Kremlin hardens its stance towards Tokyo

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-08-25

In the first half of August, the Kremlin sent Tokyo a strong political signal regarding the dispute over the Southern Kuril Islands (Japan’s Northern Territories). Between 4 and 12 August, Russia’s Pacific Fleet conducted large-scale exercises involving more than 60 vessels, including live-fire drills in the disputed waters. On 12 August, the Kremlin released remarks by Vladimir Putin, who was attending the exercises, and by the commander of the Pacific Fleet, both accusing Japan of taking unprovoked hostile actions against Russia, notably by imposing sanctions, and of becoming increasingly aggressive in the region. Putin also expressed regret that Tokyo had abandoned the Russia-friendly policy pursued by Shinzō Abe, Japan’s prime minister from 2012 to 2020, and announced plans to strengthen the Pacific Fleet.

On 13 August, for the first time in his career, Putin visited one of the islands at the centre of the territorial dispute with Japan (Iturup, known in Japan as Etorofu), prompting protests from the Japanese government, including Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi warned that Putin’s visit to the Kurils would have ‘an extremely negative impact’ on bilateral relations. His Russian counterpart, Sergei Lavrov, accused Tokyo of pursuing an ‘openly aggressive, militaristic course’ that is causing ‘serious concern’ in Russia.

item.content:encoded:
Ukraine: another corruption scandal within Zelensky’s inner circle

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-08-25

On 19 August, the National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine (NABU) announced a special operation codenamed Forrest Gump, targeting a criminal organisation allegedly run by members of the Verkhovna Rada and officials from the Office of the President of Ukraine (OPU). On the same day, investigators searched the home of OPU Deputy Head Iryna Mudra and premises linked to Vadym Stolar, a property developer and MP from the Restoration of Ukraine parliamentary group, which was established after the pro-Russian Opposition Platform – For Life was banned. Stolar is currently abroad. Former independent MP Maksym Mykytas and several Justice Ministry officials are also implicated in the case.

The individuals concerned are suspected of laundering the proceeds of crime. In June this year, 150 million hryvnias (around $3 million) was allegedly provided as bail for former Justice Minister Herman Halushchenko, who had been arrested six months earlier in connection with the so-called Midas scandal (see ‘Operation Midas: the largest corruption scandal within Zelensky’s inner circle’). Sense Bank, the former Russian-owned Alfa-Bank nationalised in 2023, was allegedly used for this purpose. The Union Civil Protection Mechanism was created as a tool for fast, targeted assistance between neighbours in response to events that exceed a single state's capacity to respond – from fires, floods and earthquakes to industrial accidents, chemical contamination or man-made disasters. The last two decades, and especially the events of recent years – the COVID-19 pandemic and the war in Ukraine – have tested it in ways its architects never anticipated: not as a single, closed-ended event, but as a prolonged, multidimensional crisis with no clear end point.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在36. Casimir Pulaski Foundation --Poland官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Defence and International Security

发布源: 36. Casimir Pulaski Foundation --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-08-25

The Pulaski Foundation Defence and Security Program provides multidisciplinary analysis of the current and emerging defense and security challenges facing the Transatlantic Alliance – with a special focus on Central and Eastern Europe.

Since 2022 the program allocates much of its resources to analysing the possible outcomes and consequences for European security of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. A special component of the program is devoted to the challenges and opportunities facing Poland’s defense policy, including modernizing of the Polish army and its industry. The main goal is to present actionable recommendations to an array of Polish stakeholders, including public administration, which could form a basis for long-term strategies for Poland in times of raising military and defense demands.

Overall, through its analysis, the program advocates for a stronger presence of NATO on the Alliance’s Eastern Flank, more developed European defence capabilities and argues for the need to provide military assistance and solid security guarantees to Ukraine.
